summary: Tree crow's nest in Hood River County, OR, rigged up in the 1930s and abandoned in the 1940s; remnants reported in 2005 and 2020.

facts.design: Crow's nest platform built into a Douglas fir
facts.status_note: The platform has decayed; boards and the remains of a ladder are reported on the tree.

access.note: Reached on foot by a short spur off the Bottle Prairie Trail #455; the Oregon Hikers guide describes the spur.

visit.trail_note: From a small parking area off Road 120 at the Bottle Prairie Trailhead, then a short spur off Bottle Prairie Trail #455

events.note: Firelookout.com says 'rigged up in the 1930's'; no exact year is given

Firelookout.com says the platform was still there in the 1980s
Forest Lookouts page reports remnants of the crow's nest still remaining on the fir
Hiker found two boards with nails leaned against a large old tree; the hiker's identification of the tree was tentative

corrections.why: A 2005 note reports remnants on the fir, and the 2020 visit and the Oregon Hikers guide describe boards and a ladder's remains. The platform itself has decayed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com's page title says 'Fire Lookout Tower', but its text describes a tree crow's nest platform, and the Forest Lookouts page places it atop a Douglas fir. No source we read describes a built tower or building.

notes_for_editor: The brief's status 'gone' conflicts with the 2005 and 2020 remnant reports; 'ruins' is proposed as a correction for a human to check. The brief's 'conflict' line says firelookout.com=standing, but the page read gives no status word; the Association list says Abandoned. The 1930 built year is the decade only. The Oregon Hikers page is undated. The 2020 tree identification is the blogger's tentative guess. Fivemile Butte is a separate lookout and is not covered here. No photo with a licence was found.
